c.name: tls_api_many_losses
c.signature: /* Test that connection establishment succeeds in presence of many losses */ int tls_api_many_losses(void)

c.name: immediate_ack_test
c.signature: /* Test the immediate ACK function. */ int immediate_ack_test(void)

c.name: stateless_reset_bad_test
c.signature: /* * Server reset negative test. * Establish a connection between server and client. * When the connection is established, fabricate a bogus server reset and * send it to the client. * Expected result: the client ignores the bogus reset. */ int stateless_reset_bad_test(void)

c.name: stateless_reset_client_test
c.signature: /* * Server reset client test. * Establish a connection between server and client. * Get the connection almost established on server, * fabricate a bogus stateless reset and * send it from the client to the server. * Expected result: the server connection ignores the bogus reset. */ int stateless_reset_client_test(void)

c.name: stateless_reset_handshake_test
c.signature: /* * Server reset handshake test. * Verify that the server does not send a reset in response to * a bogus long header packet */ int stateless_reset_handshake_test(void)

c.name: tls_retry_token_valid_test
c.signature: /* Unit test of token validation */ int tls_retry_token_valid_test(void)

c.name: tls_api_multiple_versions_test
c.signature: /* * Do a simple test for all supported versions */ int tls_api_multiple_versions_test(void)

c.name: random_public_tester_test
c.signature: /* Test that the random public generation behaves in expected ways */ int random_public_tester_test(void)

c.name: retire_cnxid_test
c.signature: /* * Perform a test of the "retire connection id" function. * The test will artificially retire connection ID on the client, * and verify that the server will refill the stash of * connection ID. */ int retire_cnxid_test(void)

c.name: not_before_cnxid_test
c.signature: /* * Perform a test of the "not before" CNXID function. * The test will artificially simulate receiving a "not before" * parameter in a new connection ID test, to check that the * old connection ID are removed and successfully replaced. */ int not_before_cnxid_test(void)

c.name: ec00_zero_test
c.signature: /* Edge case zero: verify that the common code * works. */ int ec00_zero_test(void)

c.name: eca1_amplification_loss_test
c.signature: /* Amplification test using large * server hello with losses. */ int eca1_amplification_loss_test(void)

c.name: stream_state_local_reuse_test
c.signature: /* * Regression: spurious STREAM_STATE_ERROR when reusing a closed local stream id */ int stream_state_local_reuse_test(void)

c.name: gbps_performance_test
c.signature: /* AWS like performance test * Verify that 10MB can be downloaded very fast on a low latency Gbps link. */ int gbps_performance_test(void)

c.name: bbr_asym100_test
c.signature: /* Asymmetric test. * Verify that 10MB can be downloaded reasonably fast on a low latency 10Mbps link with 100kbps return path * The buffer size is set to a high value, which allows queues to grow and delays to build up. In theory, * BBR should minimize these queues, but the test verifies that it actually does. */ int bbr_asym100_test(void)

c.name: bbr_asym100_nodelay_test
c.signature: /* Asymmetric test, no delay. * Variant in which the negotiation of delayed ACK is disabled. */ int bbr_asym100_nodelay_test(void)

c.name: bbr_asym400_test
c.signature: /* Asymmetric test. * Variant using 400 kbps return path and a 40 Mbps link */ int bbr_asym400_test(void)

c.name: l4s_reno_test
c.signature: /* This test is used for reference. Perf is bad, because each CE mark is * a congestion mark. */ int l4s_reno_test(void)

c.name: cnx_limit_test
c.signature: /*Connection limit * Test that if one attempts to create more than the set limit of * connections, it fails. This is complementary to the cnx_stress * test, which verifies that if one creates exactly the "limit" number of connections, * they all succeed. */ int cnx_limit_test(void)

c.name: cert_verify_bad_cert_test
c.signature: /* BAD CERT: the server uses the wrong certificate. */ int cert_verify_bad_cert_test(void)

c.name: cert_verify_bad_sni_test
c.signature: /* BAD SNI: the name certified in the server's certificate does not match the * SNI set by the client. Verification should fail. */ int cert_verify_bad_sni_test(void)

c.name: cert_verify_null_test
c.signature: /* NULL test: do not specify a list of root CAs. * Verfication defaults to just testing that the SNI maps the name in the certificate */ int cert_verify_null_test(void)

c.name: cert_verify_null_sni_test
c.signature: /* NULL SNI: the client does not provide an SNI. * Treated as indicating that the client does not care for the SNI. */ int cert_verify_null_sni_test(void)

c.name: cert_verify_rsa_test
c.signature: /* RSA test: the certificate specifies an RSA key, and the certificate authority is * added to the trusted list. */ int cert_verify_rsa_test(void)

c.name: cid_quiescence_test
c.signature: /* * Test CID renewal on quiescence larger than PICOQUIC_CID_REFRESH_DELAY */ int cid_quiescence_test(void)

c.name: mbedtls_load_key_fail_test
c.signature: /* * Testing of failure modes. * * Testing the various reasons why loading of key should fail: * - key file does not exist * - key file is empty, no PEM keyword * - key file does not contain a key (we use a cert file for that) * - key file is for ED25559, which is not supported */ int mbedtls_load_key_fail_test(void)

c.name: monopath_basic_test
c.signature: /* Basic connection with the multicast option enabled. */ int monopath_basic_test(void)

c.name: monopath_hole_test
c.signature: /* Testing the defense against opportunistic acks. */ int monopath_hole_test(void)

c.name: monopath_keep_alive_test
c.signature: /* test that a single path connection can be kept alive */ int monopath_keep_alive_test(void)

c.name: monopath_rotation_test
c.signature: /* Testing key rotation in monopath context. */ int monopath_rotation_test(void)

c.name: multipath_aead_test
c.signature: /* * Test the multipath variant of AEAD encrypt and decrypt. */ int multipath_aead_test(void)

c.name: multipath_sat_plus_test
c.signature: /* Simulate the combination of a satellite link and a low latency low bandwidth * terrestrial link */ int multipath_sat_plus_test(void)

c.name: multipath_renew_test
c.signature: /* Test the renewal of the connection ID on a path */ int multipath_renew_test(void)

c.name: multipath_rotation_test
c.signature: /* Test key rotation in a multipath setup */ int multipath_rotation_test(void)

c.name: multipath_break1_test
c.signature: /* Test that breaking paths are removed after some time */ int multipath_break1_test(void)

c.name: multipath_socket_error_test
c.signature: /* Test reaction to socket error on second path */ int multipath_socket_error_test(void)

c.name: multipath_socket0_error_test
c.signature: /* Test reaction to socket error on first path */ int multipath_socket0_error_test(void)

c.name: multipath_abandon_test
c.signature: /* Test that abandoned paths are removed after some time */ int multipath_abandon_test(void)

c.name: multipath_back0_test
c.signature: /* Test that after breaking path 0 we can establish a new path on the * same link when it comes back up. */ int multipath_back0_test(void)

c.name: multipath_back1_test
c.signature: /* Test that breaking paths can come back up after some time */ int multipath_back1_test(void)

c.name: multipath_nat_test
c.signature: /* Test nat traversal in a multipath setup */ int multipath_nat_test(void)

c.name: multipath_perf_test
c.signature: /* Test that a typical wifi+lte scenario provides good performance */ int multipath_perf_test(void)

c.name: multipath_just_one_test
c.signature: /* Setting the initial max patht ID to 1 should allow two paths to be created */ int multipath_just_one_test(void)

c.name: multipath_break_both_test
c.signature: /* Breaking both links at the same time. Expect the connection to break, * without crashing. */ int multipath_break_both_test(void)

c.name: cnx_stress_unit_test
c.signature: /* The unit test entry point executes the cnx stress test with a * small duration and a small number of clients, the goal being to check that * the cnx stress code actually works. */ int cnx_stress_unit_test(void)
